security_review.reason: authorization boundary — fail-closed resolution guarding a money-adjacent action class across tenant isolation

stop_conditions: authorizeTenantAction is found to need a third column beyond tenants.status and subscriptions.status
any decision-table case cannot be mapped to a test

_acceptance.A1_A3: allow path — case 3: tenant active|trialing crossed with subscription trialing|active|past_due
_acceptance.B1: missing subscriptions row → deny, case 4 fail-closed (provisioning anomaly, not 'not yet in billing')
_acceptance.B2: tenant suspended wins at step 1; step 2 is not consulted — case 1
_acceptance.B3_B4: tenant past_due|cancelled are anomaly values with no write path; still deny — case 1b
_acceptance.B5: subscription cancelled → deny, case 2b; closes the suspended→cancelled shortcut around unpaid debt
_acceptance.C1: unknown tenantId → deny fail-closed without leaking existence
_acceptance.D1: query failure → deny; an error must never collapse into allow
_acceptance.E1: competing writer holds FOR UPDATE first → re-check BLOCKS, then observes the fresh value (mirrors billing test #36)
_acceptance.E2: FOR SHARE acquired first → competing writer's SKIP LOCKED defers to the next run (mirrors #36a)
_acceptance.E3: harness must hold the competing transaction OPEN while the function reads; letting it commit first lets a plain re-SELECT pass too
_acceptance.G1: one cause-agnostic denial code; deny must not reveal which axis blocked

_evidence_rules: Cite decision-table cases by number; do not restate their content — the restatement is what goes stale.
Docs and contracts are not runtime proof. A passing test against a live Postgres is.
Do not claim CODE_READY, IMPLEMENTED or any readiness state from inside the slice; the verdict artifact is docs/slice-readiness-verdicts.md and it is authored outside the worktree.
